Continent :: chunk_0000
For other uses, see [Continent (disambiguation)](/wiki/Continent_(disambiguation) "Continent (disambiguation)").

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/97/Continental_models-Australia.gif/500px-Continental_models-Australia.gif)](/wiki/File:Continental_models-Australia.gif)

Animated, colour-coded map showing four to seven continents – depending on the [convention and model](/wiki/Boundaries_between_the_continents "Boundaries between the continents"), some continents may be consolidated or subdivided.

A **continent** is any of several large terrestrial geographical regions. Continents are generally identified by [convention](/wiki/Convention_(norm) "Convention (norm)") rather than any strict criteria. A continent could be a single large [landmass](/wiki/Landmass "Landmass"), a landmass and nearby islands either on or beyond its [continental shelf](/wiki/Continental_shelf "Continental shelf"), or a part of a larger landmass, as in the case of Asia and Europe within [Eurasia](/wiki/Eurasia "Eurasia"). Due to these varying definitions, the number of continents varies, up to seven or as few as four. Most [English-speaking countries](/wiki/English-speaking_world "English-speaking world") recognize seven continents. In order from largest to smallest in area, these seven are [Asia](/wiki/Asia "Asia"), [Africa](/wiki/Africa "Africa"), [North America](/wiki/North_America "North America"), [South America](/wiki/South_America "South America"), [Antarctica](/wiki/Antarctica "Antarctica"), [Europe](/wiki/Europe "Europe"), and [Australia](/wiki/Australia_(continent) "Australia (continent)") (or sometimes [Oceania](/wiki/Oceania "Oceania") or [Australasia](/wiki/Australasia "Australasia")). Different variations with fewer continents merge some of these regions; examples of this are merging Asia and Europe into [Eurasia](/wiki/Eurasia "Eurasia"),[[1]](#cite_note-NatlGeo1-1) North America and South America into the [Americas](/wiki/Americas "A

Yosemite's [Grizzly Giant](/wiki/Grizzly_Giant "Grizzly Giant"), a 209' tall giant sequoia, Earth's [largest tree species](/wiki/List_of_tallest_trees "List of tallest trees").[[148]](#cite_note-150) Listed as endangered by the [IUCN](/wiki/IUCN "IUCN"), most [sequoia groves](/wiki/List_of_giant_sequoia_groves "List of giant sequoia groves") have been granted protected status.[[149]](#cite_note-151)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/58/JoshuaTree_20150911.jpg/250px-JoshuaTree_20150911.jpg)](/wiki/File:JoshuaTree_20150911.jpg)

Originally utilized by [Indigenous peoples](/wiki/Indigenous_peoples_of_California "Indigenous peoples of California") as a source of food and fiber for textiles, the western Joshua Tree (*[Yucca brevifolia](/wiki/Yucca_brevifolia "Yucca brevifolia")*) is a recognizable native plant of Californian deserts and protected under the State's *Western Joshua Tree Conservation Act* of 2023.[[150]](#cite_note-152)[[151]](#cite_note-153)[[152]](#cite_note-154)

California boasts several superlatives in its collection of flora: the [largest trees](/wiki/Giant_sequoia "Giant sequoia"), the [tallest trees](/wiki/Coast_redwood "Coast redwood"), and the [oldest trees](/wiki/Pinus_longaeva "Pinus longaeva"). Saudi Arabia :: Government and politics :: Foreign relations :: part 01 :: chunk_0023
Main article: [Foreign relations of Saudi Arabia](/wiki/Foreign_relations_of_Saudi_Arabia "Foreign relations of Saudi Arabia")

The foreign policy of Saudi Arabia is officially focused on cooperation with the oil-exporting [Gulf States](/wiki/Arab_states_of_the_Persian_Gulf "Arab states of the Persian Gulf"), the unity of the [Arab world](/wiki/Arab_World "Arab World"), [Islamic solidarity](/wiki/Ummah "Ummah"), and support for the [United Nations](/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations") and multilateralism. It joined the UN in 1945[[41]](#cite_note-US_State_Dept_Saudi_Arabia-46)[[223]](#cite_note-228) and is a founding member of the [Arab League](/wiki/Arab_League "Arab League"), [Gulf Cooperation Council](/wiki/Cooperation_Council_for_the_Arab_States_of_the_Gulf "Cooperation Council for the Arab States of the Gulf"), [Muslim World League](/wiki/Muslim_World_League "Muslim World League"), and the [Organisation of Islamic Cooperation](/wiki/Organisation_of_Islamic_Cooperation "Organisation of Islamic Cooperation").[[f]](#cite_note-229)[[224]](#cite_note-Saudi_Ministry_of_Foreign_Affairs-230) Saudi Arabia joined the [World Trade Organization](/wiki/World_Trade_Organization "World Trade Organization") in 2005 and plays a prominent role in the [International Monetary Fund](/wiki/International_Monetary_Fund "International Monetary Fund"), the [World Bank](/wiki/The_World_Bank "The World Bank"), and the [G20](/wiki/G20 "G20").[[41]](#cite_note-US_State_Dept_Saudi_Arabia-46) Although part of the [Non-Aligned Movement](/wiki/Non-Aligned_Movement "Non-Aligned Movement"), Saudi Arabia is generally considered pro-Western.[[225]](#cite_note-231)

Since co-founding [OPEC](/wiki/OPEC "OPEC") in 1960, Saudi Arabia's oil pricing policy has officially aimed to stabilize the world oil market and moderate sharp price movements so as not to jeopardize Western economies.[[41]](#cite_note-US_State_Dept_

The **Colosseum** ([/ˌkɒ.lə.ˈsiː.əm/](/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English") [*KOL-ə-SEE-əm*](/wiki/Help:Pronunciation_respelling_key "Help:Pronunciation respelling key"); [Italian](/wiki/Italian_language "Italian language"): *Colosseo* [[kolosˈsɛːo]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Italian "Help:IPA/Italian")) is an [elliptical](/wiki/Ellipse "Ellipse") [amphitheatre](/wiki/Amphitheatre "Amphitheatre") in the centre of the city of [Rome](/wiki/Rome "Rome"), Italy, just east of the [Roman Forum](/wiki/Roman_Forum "Roman Forum"). It is the largest ancient amphitheatre ever built, and is the largest standing amphitheatre in the world. In 1994, [Audrey Hepburn](/wiki/Audrey_Hepburn "Audrey Hepburn") became the fifth person to win all four awards, and the first to do so posthumously.

British actress and humanitarian [Audrey Hepburn](/wiki/Audrey_Hepburn "Audrey Hepburn") (1929–1993) received her fourth distinct award [posthumously](/wiki/Posthumous_award "Posthumous award") in 1994. Between 1954 and 1994, Hepburn received a total of four competitive awards. She was the fifth person to complete the feat and the first to do so posthumously. She was also the first winner to win two of their awards in consecutive awards shows (the [1994 Grammys](/wiki/36th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "36th Annual Grammy Awards") were the first Grammys since her posthumous win at the [1993 Emmys](/wiki/45th_Primetime_Emmy_Awards "45th Primetime Emmy Awards")). She is the only EGOT winner to not win multiple awards in any of the four award fields.

* As of 2019, Box Office Mojo correctly recorded that *Titanic* had grossed $1.843 billion on its original release, $344 million from its 3D reissue in 2012, and a further $692,000 from a limited release in 2017 for a lifetime total of $2.187 billion.[[13]](#cite_note-98) Following a limited re-release in 2020, Box Office Mojo incorrectly added $7 million to the original release total.[[14]](#cite_note-99) By the end of 2021, Box Office Mojo had corrected the original release total, but added the $7 million figure to both the 2012 and 2017 reissue totals, incorrectly increasing the lifetime total by $14 million to $2.202 billion.[[15]](#cite_note-100) At the beginning of 2023, Box Office Mojo corrected the total for the 2017 reissue, bringing the lifetime gross down to $2.195 billion, but retained the error in the 2012 reissue.[[16]](#cite_note-101)
* The Numbers does not log individual releases, but had the lifetime total recorded as $2.186 billion in September 2014 (roughly equating to $1.843 billion for the original release and $343.6 million for the 3D reissue).[[17]](#cite_note-102) A couple of weeks later, The Numbers increased the lifetime gross to $2.208 billion, without explanation.[[18]](#cite_note-103)

Asia is the largest continent in the world by a considerable margin, and it is rich in natural resources, such as [petroleum](/wiki/Petroleum "Petroleum"), [forests](/wiki/Forest "Forest"), [fish](/wiki/Fish "Fish"), [water](/wiki/Water "Water"), [rice](/wiki/Rice "Rice"), [copper](/wiki/Copper "Copper") and [silver](/wiki/Silver "Silver"). Manufacturing in Asia has traditionally been strongest in East and Southeast Asia, particularly in China, [Taiwan](/wiki/Taiwan "Taiwan"), South Korea, Japan, India, the Philippines, and Singapore. Japan and South Korea continue to dominate in the area of [multinational corporations](/wiki/Multinational_corporation "Multinational corporation"), though increasingly China and India are making significant inroads. Many companies from Europe, North America, South Korea, and Japan have operations in Asia's developing countries to take advantage of its abundant supply of cheap labour and relatively developed infrastructure.[[113]](#cite_note-126)[[114]](#cite_note-127)

According to [Citigroup](/wiki/Citigroup "Citigroup") in 2011, 9 of 11 [Global Growth Generator](/wiki/3G_countries "3G countries") countries came from Asia driven by population and income growth. They are Bangladesh, China, India, Indonesia, Iraq, Mongolia, the Philippines, Sri Lanka, and Vietnam.[[115]](#cite_note-128) Asia has three main financial centers: Hong Kong, Tokyo, and Singapore. [Call centers](/wiki/Call_center "Call center") and [business process outsourcing](/wiki/Business_process_outsourcing "Business process outsourcing") firms (BPOs) are becoming major employers in India and the Philippines due to the availability of a large pool of highly skilled, English-speaking workers. The increased use of outsourcing has assisted the rise of India and the China as financial centers. Due to its large and extremely competitive information technology industry, India has become a major hub for outsourcing.[[116]](#cite_note-12

The moons of Jupiter are listed below by orbital period. Moons massive enough for their surfaces to have [collapsed](/wiki/Hydrostatic_equilibrium "Hydrostatic equilibrium") into a [spheroid](/wiki/Spheroid "Spheroid") are highlighted in bold. These are the four [Galilean moons](/wiki/Galilean_moons "Galilean moons"), which are comparable in size to the [Moon](/wiki/Moon "Moon"). The other moons are much smaller. The Galilean moon with the smallest amount of mass is greater than 7,000 times more massive than the most massive of the other moons.[[6]](#cite_note-jpllist-7) The [irregular](/wiki/Irregular_satellite "Irregular satellite") captured moons are shaded light gray and orange when [prograde](/wiki/Direct_motion "Direct motion") and yellow, red, and dark gray when [retrograde](/wiki/Retrograde_motion "Retrograde motion"). The orbits and mean distances of the irregular moons are highly variable over short timescales due to frequent planetary and solar [perturbations](/wiki/Perturbation_(astronomy) "Perturbation (astronomy)"),[[36]](#cite_note-Brozovic2017-37) so [proper orbital elements](/wiki/Proper_orbital_elements "Proper orbital elements") which are averaged over a period of time are preferably used.
